DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO. FEB 2 6 2025 HON. JUNIO C. DUALAN Vice Mayor Municipality of Naic Province of Cavite Dear Vice Mayor Dualan: This has reference to your letter dated 11 December 2024 seeking this Departments confirmatory legal opinion on the following matters: I. That the quorum needed for Sangguniang Bayan of Naic is six (6) given the total membership of Sangguniang Bayan is eleven (I I), consisting of eight (8) elected councilors, two (2) ex-officio members, and the Vice-Mayor as Presiding Officer; and 2. That in the reclassification of agricultural lands under Section 20 of R.A. No. 7160, the ordinance to be enacted by the Sanggunian authorizing the reclassification of agricultural lands requires only simple majority, i.e., majority votes of the Sanggunian members present, there being a quorum. As to the first query, we answer in the affirmative. In this regard, we would like to inform you that this Department have already rendered opinions on the same subject matter in DILG Opinion No. 04 series of 2020, and DILG Opinion No 122 series of 2022. In the said opinions, we opined that a quorum is defined as the presence of the majority of all members of the sanggunian who have been duly elected and qualified, and that when determining a quorum in the sanggunian, a majority of all members of the sanggunian who have been elected shall constitute a quorum. Further, the Presiding Officer should only be counted for purposes of ascertaining the existence of a quorum, but not in the determination of the required number of votes necessary to uphold a matter before the sanggunian. As to the second query, we also answer in the affirmative. This Department opines that the majority vote required by law is only simple majority. Article 107 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the Local Government Code provides that no ordinance passed by the sanggunian shall be valid unless approved by a majority of the members present, there being a quorum. However, Article 38 of the IRR likewise provides that a municipality may only reclassify agricultural lands through an ordinance after conducting public hearings for the purpose provided that there exists an approved zoning ordinance implementing its comprehensive land use plan. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LRALLDnasm Page 2 of 2
